chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Abdullah ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Aban, from Zurara, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them), who said:
The black dogs, the beasts, are from the Jinn.
ai.seo_question: What is the nature of black dogs in Shia hadith cosmology?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi identifies black dogs as 'behem' (beasts) of the jinn, a classification rooted in Shia tradition that distinguishes them from other canine types based on their spiritual nature. The chain of narration (isnad) traces back to Imam al-Sadiq (AS), emphasizing the authority of the Ahl al-Bayt in defining ritual purity (taharah) and the metaphysical characteristics of animals. This view informs Shia fiqh regarding the impurity (najis) status of black dogs and their role in the unseen world.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, and Muhammad Bin yahya, from Abdullah Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Aban, from Zurara, 
(It has been narrated) from one of the two (5<sup>th</sup> or 6<sup>th</sup> Imam<sup>asws</sup>) having said: ‘
The dogs, entirely black, are from the Jinn’.
en.sarwar: 7. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from and Muhammad ibn Yahya from ‘Abd Allah ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Aban from Zurarah who has said the following: “One of the two Imam, (abu Ja‘far or abu ‘Abd Allah), ‘Alayhim al-Salam, has said that
dogs of one color, all black are from Jinn.’”
